criteria.description: `requireJwt` is added to `src/middleware/auth.ts`. It verifies the Bearer token using `verifyJwt`, attaches `req.user = { userId }` on success, and calls `next()`. When the token is absent or invalid it responds with HTTP 401 and calls no further handlers. It must not modify `requireAuth`.
criteria.evidence: auth.ts lines 51-68: `requireJwt` exported, extracts Bearer token, calls `verifyJwt(token)`, sets `req.user = { userId: payload.userId }`, calls `next()`. Lines 55-63: absent or invalid token → `res.status(401).json({ error: 'Unauthorized' })` with no further handlers. `requireAuth` (lines 21-49) is unmodified. Tests for reqs 4, 5, 9, 10, 11, 12 all pass (all send Bearer tokens and succeed); test 'requires a valid JWT' passes returning 401 without token.

criteria.description: `src/types/express.d.ts` declares `user?: { userId: string }` on the Express `Request` interface so `req.user.userId` compiles without `any` or `@ts-ignore`.
criteria.evidence: express.d.ts line 6: `user?: { userId: string };` inside `namespace Express { interface Request { ... } }`. `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` exited with code 0 (no output, no errors).

criteria.description: `GET /api/auth/me` is routed through `requireJwt` and its controller reads the user exclusively from `req.user!.userId`. A request carrying a spoofed id in the query string still returns only the token owner's data.
criteria.evidence: authRoutes.ts line 11: `router.get('/me', requireJwt, me)`. authController.ts line 29: `const user = getUserById(req.user!.userId)` — no query-string param access anywhere. Test 'returns only the caller's own data regardless of a spoofed id in the URL' → ✓ passed (136ms).

criteria.description: `PATCH /api/users/me` requires a valid JWT. Any request without a valid `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header returns HTTP 401.
criteria.evidence: userRoutes.ts line 9: `router.patch('/me', requireJwt, validate(userUpdateSchema), updateMe)`. Test 'requires a valid JWT' → ✓ passed (2ms), unauthenticated PATCH returned 401.

criteria.description: `PATCH /api/users/me` with a valid JWT and body `{ username: "new_value" }` returns HTTP 200 with JSON body `{ user: { id, email, username, createdAt } }` where `user.username` equals the new value, `user.email` is unchanged, and `user` does not contain a `password` field.
criteria.evidence: userController.ts line 12: `res.json({ user })` where `user` is `toUserResponse(row)` from userService.ts lines 27-29 (only id, email, username, createdAt — no password). Test 'updates the username and returns the new user object' → ✓ passed (55ms).

criteria.description: `PATCH /api/users/me` with an empty body `{}` or a body with no recognised fields returns HTTP 400.
criteria.evidence: userSchema.ts lines 10-16: first `.refine()` requires at least one of username/email/currentPassword/newPassword to be present, driving 400 via validate middleware. Test 'returns 400 for an empty body / no recognised fields' → ✓ passed (55ms).

criteria.description: `PATCH /api/users/me` with `{ newPassword: "..." }` but no `currentPassword` field returns HTTP 400.
criteria.evidence: userSchema.ts lines 18-20: second `.refine()` enforces `!data.newPassword || data.currentPassword !== undefined`. Test 'returns 400 when newPassword is given without currentPassword' → ✓ passed (55ms).

criteria.description: `PATCH /api/users/me` with `{ currentPassword, newPassword }` where `currentPassword` does not match the stored bcrypt hash returns HTTP 400 with JSON body `{ "error": "Current password is incorrect" }`.
criteria.evidence: userService.ts lines 39-43: `compare(updates.currentPassword, currentRow.password)` → if false, throws `AppError('Current password is incorrect', 400, 'INVALID_PASSWORD')`. Test 'returns 400 "Current password is incorrect" when currentPassword is wrong' → ✓ passed (107ms). Stderr confirms AppError with message 'Current password is incorrect'.

criteria.description: `PATCH /api/users/me` with correct `currentPassword` and `newPassword` updates the stored password such that old password login returns 401 and new password login returns 200.
criteria.evidence: userService.ts lines 65-67: hashes new password with `hash(updates.newPassword, 10)` and includes in single UPDATE. Test 'updates the password so a subsequent login with the new password succeeds and the old one fails' → ✓ passed (263ms). Stderr shows 'Invalid credentials' AppError triggered for old password login (expected).

criteria.description: After a successful password update, the `password` column stores a bcrypt hash matching `/^\$2[aby]?\$/`.
criteria.evidence: userService.ts line 66: `hash(updates.newPassword, 10)` (bcryptjs produces `$2b$` prefix). Test 'stores the updated password as a bcrypt hash, not plaintext' → ✓ passed (157ms).

criteria.description: `PATCH /api/users/me` with an email already owned by a different user returns HTTP 409. When the body also includes a username change, neither the email nor the username is written — the update is fully atomic.
criteria.evidence: userService.ts lines 46-53: email conflict checked before building UPDATE; lines 55-62: username conflict also checked; line 87: a single `UPDATE users SET ... WHERE id = ?` issued only after all checks pass. Test 'returns 409 for an email already taken by another user, and leaves no field changed' → ✓ passed (109ms). Stderr confirms AppError EMAIL_CONFLICT at statusCode 409.

criteria.description: `PATCH /api/users/me` with a username already owned by a different user returns HTTP 409.
criteria.evidence: userService.ts lines 55-62: username conflict check throws `AppError('Username already taken', 409, 'USERNAME_CONFLICT')`. Test 'returns 409 for a username already taken by another user' → ✓ passed (111ms). Stderr confirms AppError USERNAME_CONFLICT at statusCode 409.

criteria.description: The `password` field does not appear in any API response from `GET /api/auth/me` or `PATCH /api/users/me`.
criteria.evidence: userService.ts `toUserResponse` (lines 27-29) returns only {id, email, username, createdAt}. authController.ts `me` calls `getUserById` (excludes password). Test 'updates the username and returns the new user object' asserts `res.body.user.password === undefined` → ✓ passed. All 44 tests pass with 0 failures.

criteria.description: A Zod validation schema for the PATCH body exists at `src/schemas/userSchema.ts`. Treats all four fields as optional, rejects a body with none of them, and enforces that `newPassword` requires `currentPassword`.
criteria.evidence: userSchema.ts: exports `userUpdateSchema` (z.object with username/email/currentPassword/newPassword all optional), two `.refine()` calls — first enforces at least one field, second enforces currentPassword when newPassword present. Tests for reqs 6 and 7 pass (400 responses). `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` exits 0.

criteria.description: The `updateUser(userId, updates)` function in `src/services/userService.ts` performs uniqueness validation and all field writes as a single atomic SQL UPDATE (one statement).
criteria.evidence: userService.ts lines 69-88: builds `setClauses` and `values` arrays from all update fields, then issues a single `db.prepare('UPDATE users SET ... WHERE id = ?').run(...values)` on line 87. Test for req 11 'returns 409 for an email already taken by another user, and leaves no field changed' → ✓ passed (109ms), confirming no partial write before conflict check.
